overall_assessment: The PEAD memo's numbers are correct and free of look-ahead. From the raw SEC submissions files and daily bars, with code written before opening PEAD_run.py, I reproduce every TEST cell to within rounding: C1 h=5 -0.171% (claimed -0.167), C1 h=20 +0.094% (0.098), C2 h=20 +0.746% (0.746, exact n), C2 h=5 -0.100% (exact), C3 h=20 +0.645% (0.658), and the un-registered h=1 cells (+0.267% / +0.278%). The only systematic difference is a month-quintile boundary convention (pandas rank(pct=True) with q>0.8 vs my (rank-1)/n>=0.8), which adds 96 boundary events to their C1/C3 sets and moves means by <=0.013 pp; the prereg did not pin the convention, and neither choice changes any verdict. Look-ahead audit: all 40 randomly sampled trades pass all 20 checks (ET conversion, timing, R mapping, prev-close and ADV20 filters computed through R-1, tier cost, close_R, open_{R+1}, reaction/gap/volratio, C1/C2 flags, ret/spy/net at h=5 and 20, ce=net-ctrl); over the whole 32,452-row file, my independent R/timing/ticker mapping agrees on 100% of rows, ADV20(R-1) matches to 1e-6 on 100%, filters hold on 100%, and there are 0 dedupe violations. Control construction was verified both empirically (candidate pools identical to mine: n_ctrl matches 99.9%, exact control-return agreement wherever fewer than 5 candidates exist) and by reading PEAD_run.py after the fact (base = eligible & ~evwin, i.e. no 8-K 2.02 reaction day within +-5 sessions; entry at Open_{R+1}; controls charged their own tier). Preregistration hash matches PEAD_prereg_sha256.txt (e836e79f...), written 3 minutes before the first output. Survivorship caveat is stated in the report (line 259) and in the prereg; things_tried.csv carries 106 PEAD rows covering all 8 family cells and the descriptive variants (I appended 4 VPEAD rows). Substantively: for the operator's question, the most robust news-conditioned continuation anomaly in the literature (PEAD) does not survive retail costs in this 2015-2026 US large/mid-cap universe at 5-20 days, and matched non-event names with the same day-0 move do as well or better, so the earnings news itself adds nothing beyond the move. The only intervals clear of zero are 1-day effects of roughly +0.27% net (losers keep falling on R+1; big-beat names drift up on R+1), which were not pre-registered, are one-day-of-costs thin, and (for the short side) are flattered by survivorship. Nothing here supports building a real-time news-momentum system; if the h=1 cells are to be pursued they need a fresh pre-registration on data not yet used (post-2026-08 only), a delisting-inclusive universe, and borrow costs for the short side.
concerns: Month-quintile rank convention not specified in the prereg: PEAD_run.py uses pandas rank(pct=True) with q>0.8 (1-based rank/n); an equally valid (rank-1)/n>=0.8 removes 96 boundary events from C1 and adds 96 to C3. Immaterial to conclusions (Δmean <= 0.013 pp) but should be pinned in future registrations.

Matched-control test is underpowered: only 22.6% of C1 events and 5.9% of C2 events have any control within 1 pp of day-0 excess in the same ADV decile; control-excess CIs are +-2 pp (C1) and +-9 pp (C2). The 'news or move?' answer for C1 (controls do as well) is directional, not precise. The anydecile sensitivity run exists but I did not recompute it.

Survivorship is stated but not quantified: 1,008 of 5,213 8-K 2.02 filers have no bar file (delisted/non-universe), and the un-registered C3 short h=1 result is the cell most inflated by their absence; the h=1 long cells are mildly inflated too.

The descriptive h=1 cells (C3 short +0.27% [0.14,0.40], C2 +0.28% [0.04,0.53]) are the only intervals clear of zero and are not in the Holm family; they must not be reported as findings without a new pre-registration on unused data (only post-2026-08 remains) and short-side borrow costs.

The month-quintile threshold uses later events in the same month (disclosed mild look-ahead); I did not independently recompute the C1_trail trailing-threshold variant, so its look-ahead-free status rests on PEAD_run.py's own code (l.276: shift(1).rolling(250).quantile(0.8), which is correctly lagged on inspection).

Weekend/holiday filings between 09:30 and 16:00 ET are labelled 'intra' by PEAD_run.py (l.146 does not check trading-day status) though R is still the next session; my labelling differs on those rows but the trades file's timing column matched mine on 100% of rows, so no such filings survived the filters.
